objectives: To analyze the asymptotic performance of classical and modern computer algorithms.
To demonstrate proficiency in applying divide-and-conquer, greedy, and dynamic programming paradigms.
To synthesize graph-theoretic models for network flow and traversal optimization.
To understand complexity hierarchies, tractability, and polynomial-time reductions for NP-Complete problems.

course_outcomes.statement: Explain asymptotic complexity notations, recurrence relations, and algorithmic efficiency models across best, average, and worst-case bounds.
Apply divide-and-conquer, greedy selection, and dynamic programming techniques to solve constrained algorithmic optimization problems.
Analyze minimum spanning tree, shortest path, and maximum network flow algorithms on sparse and dense graph topologies.
Differentiate polynomial vs non-deterministic polynomial problem classes (P, NP, NP-Complete) using formal reduction proofs.
Evaluate randomized and approximation heuristics for computationally intractable NP-hard combinatorial bottlenecks.
Design branch-and-bound and state-space search architectures for high-dimensional computational decision systems.

mapping_justifications.CO1-PO1: Mathematical induction and asymptotic recurrence analysis form the bedrock of fundamental engineering knowledge.
mapping_justifications.CO2-PO3: Formulating dynamic programming matrices directly exercises solution design for complex constrained engineering systems.
mapping_justifications.CO3-PO4: Investigating network flow bounds against min-cut capacity involves rigorous analytical verification.
mapping_justifications.CO4-PO2: NP-completeness classification enforces deep problem-hardness formulation and mathematical reduction.
mapping_justifications.CO5-PO5: Utilizing approximation algorithms requires software modeling tools and empirical benchmark simulations.
mapping_justifications.CO6-PSO1: Branch-and-bound search synthesis directly delivers core algorithmic software engineering competency.

syllabus_units.title: Introduction & Asymptotic Analysis
syllabus_units.topics: Order Notation (O, Omega, Theta), Master Theorem, Substitution Method, Recursion Tree, Recurrences, Amortized Analysis (Accounting & Potential Methods).

syllabus_units.title: Divide & Conquer and Greedy Paradigms
syllabus_units.topics: Strassen Matrix Multiplication, Convex Hull, Greedy Choice Property, Optimal Substructure, Fractional Knapsack, Huffman Coding, Job Sequencing with Deadlines.

syllabus_units.title: Dynamic Programming & Graph Algorithms
syllabus_units.topics: Matrix Chain Multiplication, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), 0/1 Knapsack, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Johnson Algorithm, Maximum Bipartite Matching, Ford-Fulkerson.

syllabus_units.title: Tractability & NP-Completeness
syllabus_units.topics: Deterministic vs Non-deterministic Turing Machines, Polynomial Reductions, Cook-Levin Theorem, Satisfiability (3-SAT), Clique, Vertex Cover, Hamiltonian Cycle, TSP.

syllabus_units.title: Approximation, Randomized & Branch-and-Bound
syllabus_units.topics: Approximation Ratio, Vertex Cover 2-Approximation, Metric TSP, Random Treaps, Quickselect Expected Bounds, Branch and Bound LC-Search, 15-Puzzle Problem, Assignment Problem.
